summary: This document is a pipeline update for the KISS1R program, describing a Generation-2 design pivot following selectivity learnings from the Generation-1 (C1) computational library. Key findings include identification of a cross-reactivity liability with NPFFR1/NPFFR2 receptors and two engineered mechanisms (Trp10 substitution and Cit9) to address it. The program is transitioning from computational screening (Gates 1–8) toward wet-lab validation (Gate 9) at Adaptyv Bio, with C1-01 as the primary lead.

content_blocks.title: Overview
content_blocks.content: Following the successful publication of the Generation-1 (C1) computational library, the KISS1R program has evolved through a critical learning phase. Recent selectivity assessment at Gate 8 has produced sharp mechanistic insights, triggering a coordinated pivot into Generation 2. This new phase comprises three parallel tracks: (1) a cleanup of the C1 library, (2) a rational C2 redesign library, and (3) a diversity-focused C3 RFdiffusion discovery library. The program is entirely computational at this stage, with wet-lab validation (Gate 9) as the next step.

content_blocks.title: Generation-1 Selectivity Learning
content_blocks.content: Selectivity analysis revealed that the canonical C-terminal -RF amide motif (shared with endogenous NPFF/NPAF ligands) represents a significant cross-reactivity liability for NPFFR1 and NPFFR2. Specific failures: C1-02 failed G8 selectivity (NPFFR1 ddG of -0.70 kcal/mol vs KISS1R), confirmed across multiple Boltz2 runs. C1-05 and C1-06 similarly fell below the +1.4 kcal/mol selectivity threshold. Structural determinant identified: KISS1R features Ala287 at BW position 6.59, while NPFFR1 and NPFFR2 possess Asp residues at the same position. Two orthogonal selectivity mechanisms were designed: (1) Trp10 Substitution — bulky indole sterically hinders the salt-bridge contact required by NPFFR Asp residues while leaving KISS1R binding unaffected; (2) Cit9 Mechanism — replacing Arg9 guanidinium with neutral ureido (Citrulline) eliminates the cationic interaction that NPFFRs require.

content_blocks.title: Generation 2 Active Tracks
content_blocks.content:
Library | Strategy | Selectivity Approach | Status
C2 | Rational redesign of C1 | Trp10, Triazole backbones, N-Me scans | C2-01 cleared G1–G7
C3 | RFdiffusion discovery | 20% explicit selectivity weighting | C3-04 active; C3-02 dropped

Designed between May 2 and May 4, 2026.

content_blocks.title: Lead Progress
content_blocks.content:
C2-01 (C1-01 backbone with Phe10→Trp10 substitution) is the highest-confidence C2 entry. Cleared G1 through G7 with strong metrics: G4 dG -13.10 kcal/mol; G5 peptide RMSD 2.015 Å. G8 selectivity testing is pending final sequence verification.

C1-01 has cleared all eight computational gates and is staging for Adaptyv G9 validation. Carries a minor NPFFR2 flag (ddG +0.86); proceeding to functional assays to address experimentally.

C1-10 is currently undergoing high-fidelity MD (G5 v2) to test the Cit9 hypothesis with explicit parameterization.

content_blocks.title: Candidate Status Summary
content_blocks.content:
Candidate | Status | Reason
C1-01 | STAGING G9 | Cleared all 8 gates; primary lead for wet-lab.
C1-02 | STAGING G9 | Progressing to wet-lab for selectivity 'truth function' testing.
C1-03/04 | DROPPED | Insufficient predicted affinity (G4).
C1-05/06 | DROPPED | Failed selectivity criteria (G8).
C1-07/08 | PRE-DROPPED | Redundant mechanism; insights folded into C2.
C3-02 | DROPPED | Intrinsically disordered oscillation at G2.

Note: Even the native KP-10 reference fails stability gates (G6), confirming the pipeline identifies only genuine improvements over the natural parent.

content_blocks.title: Next Steps: Wet-Lab Validation
content_blocks.content: Transitioning from computational design to physical validation with an evidence-first approach. C1-02 will be evaluated against an NPFFR1/NPFFR2 BLI (Bio-Layer Interferometry) panel at Adaptyv Bio alongside the target KISS1R. Philosophy: 'Wet-lab is the truth function for selectivity predictions. Do not pre-judge.' Full experimental readouts from Generation 1 leads and first Generation 2 results are expected in the coming weeks.

key_findings: Program is entirely computational (TRL 2–3 boundary); no wet-lab data reported yet — Gate 9 (Adaptyv Bio BLI assay) is the first planned experimental validation.
C1-01 is the primary lead: cleared all 8 computational gates; staging for Adaptyv G9 wet-lab validation; minor NPFFR2 selectivity flag (ddG +0.86 kcal/mol).
C1-02 failed G8 selectivity (NPFFR1 ddG -0.70 kcal/mol vs KISS1R) but is still being sent to wet-lab as a selectivity 'truth function' control.
Selectivity threshold is +1.4 kcal/mol; C1-05 and C1-06 dropped for failing this threshold.
Structural basis for selectivity identified: KISS1R Ala287 (BW 6.59) vs. NPFFR1/NPFFR2 Asp at same position — exploited via Trp10 steric clash and Cit9 charge elimination.
C2-01 (Phe10→Trp10 substitution on C1-01 backbone) cleared G1–G7: G4 dG -13.10 kcal/mol, G5 peptide RMSD 2.015 Å; G8 pending.
C1-10 undergoing high-fidelity MD (G5 v2) to test Cit9 hypothesis with explicit parameterization.
C3 library uses RFdiffusion with 20% explicit selectivity weighting; C3-04 active, C3-02 dropped for intrinsic disorder at G2.
Native KP-10 reference peptide fails stability gate G6, validating pipeline stringency.
Computational tools used include Boltz2 (selectivity ddG calculations) and MD simulations; wet-lab platform is Adaptyv Bio BLI.
